bull.b: SenesTech’s proprietary fertility-control approach is a durable competitive position versus toxicants/traps. It aligns with public-health and ESG preferences, supports institutional contracts, and creates repeat purchase economics from ongoing deployments, reducing commodity pricing pressure.

bull.t: Growing recurring revenue and multi-channel traction
bull.b: Acceleration in D2C, subscription and B2B channels indicates stronger customer acquisition and recurring revenue potential. Diversified channels reduce single-channel risk, improve lifetime value, and provide a clearer path to scale marketing spend and convert trial momentum into sustainable revenues.

Substantial margin expansion reflects better pricing, mix, and manufacturing/fulfillment efficiency. Higher gross margins create durable operating leverage potential as sales scale, improving the path to profitability and making incremental revenue far more valuable to cash-flow conversion.

bear.t: Persistent negative cash flow and burn
bear.b: Ongoing multi-year cash burn forces reliance on external financing and limits strategic optionality. Until FCF turns sustainably positive, growth initiatives may be constrained, dilution risk remains, and management must prioritize cash efficiency over faster market share capture.

bear.t: Large operating/net losses and weak ROE
bear.b: Very large losses and negative returns are eroding equity and reduce financial flexibility. Persistent unprofitability increases refinancing risk, pressures margins from needed SG&A investment, and raises the bar for management to deliver sustained scale to achieve acceptable returns.

bear.t: Structural limits to rapid geographic/retail expansion
bear.b: Lengthy regulatory processes and the need to build brand awareness before retail rollouts slow scalable expansion. These structural constraints make scaling outside core markets capital and time intensive, delaying revenue diversification and amplifying the need for focused, efficient market entry.
